audit.whatIsWrong: The win-rate sources straddle even: MC_WR_TABLES.sejuani.kled is 47.3 over 148 games, the packet says 51.11 over 45. One is a losing lane, the other is a winning one.
audit.why: The page is built as a losing lane, which suits 47.3. The gap is small enough that no individual claim on the page turns on it, so I corrected mechanics freely but changed no stage side or difficulty rating.
audit.corrected: Nothing on ratings. Recorded as a question.

audit.why: The stage sides and captions agree with each other here, which is not true of most of this slice. Kled owns levels 1-5 on Bear Trap on a Rope plus the Skaarl health bar; Level 6 is Skill because Glacial Prison finally answers his charge; and the item stages stay his because his damage does not fall off before Sejuani's second item. Nothing needed re-siding.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two ability names are wrong throughout. The page writes 'Beartrap on a Rope' in whys[1], spikes[0], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]; Riot's name is 'Bear Trap on a Rope', two words. The page writes 'Chaaaaarge!!!' in whys[4], spikes[1], wants.foe[2], mid and late; Riot's name is 'Chaaaaaaaarge!!!'. Separately, nothing on the page mentions that his ultimate grants a shield — Riot's text: 'Kled and Skaarl charge to a location, leaving a speed-granting trail behind them and gaining a shield.'
audit.why: The names are the class of error this project's calibration list exists to catch. The shield is the mechanical gap and it costs kills: the page tells Sejuani to intercept his charge with Glacial Prison, but she arrives into a shielded Kled, so a burst that looks lethal on paper does not land. Knowing the shield is there turns the play from 'burst him as he arrives' into 'stun him, let the shield expire, then commit'. Bear Trap also slows, and Fury of the North grants immunity to slows while Frost Armor holds — so the hook's damage and yank land but its slow does not.
audit.corrected: Both names corrected in every field I opened; the R shield is now stated in spikes[1] and mid; the slow immunity is in wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears anywhere on this page. early says to trade 'only if he's already burned Q' without saying how long that buys, and mid tells you to watch his courage bar with no clock at all.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11 seconds at rank 1 down to 7, Jousting is 13 down to 9, Violent Tendencies is 13 down to 9, and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140 at rank 1. The eleven seconds after a missed hook is the entire trading window this lane offers Sejuani, and the page gestures at it without ever naming it.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap's 11s, Jousting's 13s and the ultimate's 140s are now in early, mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: Violent Tendencies is described as a burst but never as an auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Riot: 'Kled gains massive attack speed for four attacks. The fourth attack deals more damage.' It is an auto reset, so the damage arrives on the swing rather than on the cast — the wind-up is the cue to step back, and the fourth swing is the one to avoid rather than the first.

edits.after: Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) comes online at 11 seconds a cast, and a landed hook yanks you into burst range before your full combo exists.

edits.before: Kled's Violent Tendencies (W) burst at Level 3 trades favorably into your Q-W-E window; he has the mounted courage to stay and fight the stun.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies (W) is an auto reset — the fourth swing is the big one, so read the wind-up. Mounted, he has the courage to eat your stun.

edits.after: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! (R) and Jousting (E) give him a gap-close that beats your Q angle, and the R shields him on arrival — he picks.

edits.after: Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) online at 11 seconds — a landed hook pulls you into Violent Tendencies, an auto reset whose fourth swing does the real damage.

edits.after: Land Bear Trap on a Rope (Q) to yank you into Violent Tendencies (W) and knock Skaarl's courage down

edits.before: At Level 1 you have nothing but W and the threat of Frost stacks — Kled has his Q hook and a remount mechanic that means every trade he picks he's already budgeted a second HP bar for. Take W, farm the wave at the tips of your ice shards, and accept that he controls the brush. The moment he flashes his Q animation, walk toward your tower side wall: the hook pulls you toward him, so lateral positioning is your only dodge. At Level 3 your full combo (Q knock-up, W double-strike, E stun) is online, but Kled's Violent Tendencies burst at Level 3 can out-damage the stun window entirely — trade only if he's already burned Q and you've pre-stacked Frost with a W first-strike.
edits.after: At Level 1 you have W and the threat of Frost stacks; Kled has a hook and a second health bar he has already budgeted into every trade he picks. Take W, farm at the tips of your ice shards, and accept that he owns the brush. When you see the Q animation, walk toward your tower-side wall — the hook pulls you toward him, so lateral positioning is the only dodge, and Frost Armor's slow immunity means the trap's slow never lands even when the yank does. Bear Trap on a Rope is 11 seconds at rank 1: a miss is your whole trading window. At Level 3 your Q knock-up into W double-strike into Permafrost is online, but his W out-damages the stun — go only on a spent hook with Frost pre-stacked.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the worst window: Kled remounts faster than you heal, his W shreds through your early resistances before Sunfire exists, and your Q engage is readable enough that he can step aside and punish the landing lag. Play the far side of the wave, track his courage bar visually (dismounted Kled is a kill, mounted Kled is a threat), and call your jungler for a gank on dismount — that's the only reliable way to convert this window. At Level 6 your dynamic shifts: Glacial Prison gives you a ranged CC answer to his charge angle. When you see him wind up Chaaaaarge!!!, throw R early so the comet intercepts him in the channel, not after he's already in your face with full courage.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the worst window: he remounts faster than you heal, his W shreds your resistances before Sunfire exists, and your Q engage is readable enough that he steps aside and punishes the landing. Play the far side of the wave, watch the courage bar — dismounted Kled is a kill, mounted Kled is a threat — and call your jungler on the dismount. Jousting is 13 seconds at rank 1, so a spent E is a real window. At Level 6 Glacial Prison answers his charge angle, but Chaaaaaaaarge!!! shields him on arrival, so freeze him first and let the shield burn off before you commit the chain. At 140 seconds, a spent ultimate is the safest lane you will get.

edits.before: - Kled Beartrap on a Rope: matchup-defining — The hook starts his all-in — dodge it and disengage his remount. Count it out loud if you must. - Your Q dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Kled Bear Trap on a Rope: matchup-defining — 11s at rank 1 down to 7s. A missed hook is your whole trade window. - Jousting is 13s; a spent E means he cannot re-engage. - Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140s and shields him on arrival, so stun first and commit second.

edits.before: Track Kled’s Beartrap on a Rope: The hook starts his all-in — dodge it and disengage his remount. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11s and its slow does nothing through Frost Armor — only the yank lands. Violent Tendencies is an auto reset: watch the swing.

edits.before: - Sejuani vs Kled - Track: Kled Beartrap on a Rope. - Trade only through full Permafrost chains. - No commits into Beartrap on a Rope. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Sejuani vs Kled - Track: Bear Trap on a Rope, 11s. - His R shields him on arrival — stun first, burst second. - Dismounted Kled is a kill. - Hold the ult for names, not waves.

notes: Win-rate sources straddle even here (MC_WR_TABLES 47.3 over 148 games versus the packet's 51.11 over 45), so no rating or side changed. The two misspellings are widespread: 'Beartrap on a Rope' and 'Chaaaaarge!!!' also survive in wants.foe[2] and late, which I had no separate factual reason to open, so a name-only sweep is still worth running across this matchup. Not asserted: whether Glacial Prison can interrupt Chaaaaaaaarge!!! mid-charge. The current mid text implied it by telling the player to intercept him 'in the channel', but Riot's text does not describe the ultimate as a channel and kled.json carries no channel flag, so I rewrote that line to say freeze and wait out the shield rather than promise an interrupt. If the ultimate can in fact be stopped mid-charge, that is a better play and the line should be strengthened.
